You are working on the Nxeon hosting platform at /opt/nxeon-staging (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres).

CRITICAL RULES:
- NEVER run `npm run build` in /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging 
- NEVER use `git add -A` or `git add .`
- Work only in /opt/nxeon-staging

## Task: Build the Update Notifications System

The schema is already pushed. These models exist in prisma/schema.prisma:
- `UpdateAnnouncement` (id, title, body (Markdown), serviceTypes String[], screenshotUrl, status DRAFT|PUBLISHED, publishedAt, createdAt, updatedAt, seenBy)
- `UserAnnouncementSeen` (id, userId, announcementId, seenAt, @@unique([userId, announcementId]))
- User model has `announcementsSeen UserAnnouncementSeen[]` relation

### What to build:

**1. Server Actions** — Create `/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/actions-announcements.ts`:
- `listAnnouncements()` — admin: list all announcements ordered by createdAt desc
- `createAnnouncement(formData)` — admin: create with title, body, serviceTypes[], screenshotUrl. Status = DRAFT
- `publishAnnouncement(id)` — admin: set status=PUBLISHED, publishedAt=now(). This is the approval gate.
- `unpublishAnnouncement(id)` — admin: revert to DRAFT
- `deleteAnnouncement(id)` — admin: delete
- `getUnseenAnnouncements()` — customer: get PUBLISHED announcements the current user hasn't seen, filtered by serviceTypes matching their actual services. To determine what services a user has: check if they have any Server rows (VPS/GAME), HostingAccount rows (HOSTING), etc. An announcement with empty serviceTypes[] is shown to everyone.
- `markAnnouncementSeen(announcementId)` — customer: upsert UserAnnouncementSeen
- `getWhatsNew(serviceFilter?)` — customer: get all PUBLISHED announcements, optionally filtered by service type, ordered by publishedAt desc, with a `seen` boolean flag

**2. Admin UI** — Create `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/admin/announcements/page.tsx`:
- List all announcements with status badges (DRAFT = amber, PUBLISHED = green)
- Create form: title input, body textarea (Markdown), service type multi-select checkboxes (GAME, VPS, HOSTING, MAIL), optional screenshot URL
- Publish/Unpublish/Delete buttons
- Preview of the Markdown body
- Use "use server" actions pattern consistent with the rest of the admin (check existing admin pages like /opt/nxeon-staging/app/admin/ for the pattern — they use requireAdmin() from lib/auth)

**3. Customer Login Popup** — Create `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/AnnouncementPopup.tsx`:
- Client component that fetches unseen announcements on mount
- Shows a modal/popup with the announcement title, rendered Markdown body, and screenshot if present
- "Got it" button that marks it as seen and closes
- If multiple unseen, show them one at a time
- Only shows once per announcement per user (the seen tracking handles this)
- Style it to match Nxeon's dark theme (navy-900, brand-500 purple accents, white text)

**4. What's New Tab** — Create `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/WhatsNew.tsx`:
- Component that shows all published announcements in a timeline/feed layout
- Service type filter tabs at the top (All, Game Servers, VPS, Hosting)
- Each announcement shows: title, date, body (rendered Markdown), screenshot
- "New" badge on announcements the user hasn't seen yet
- Call markAnnouncementSeen when an unseen announcement scrolls into view or is clicked

**5. Wire the popup** — Add the AnnouncementPopup to the dashboard layout. Read `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/dashboard/layout.tsx` to find where to add it (it should render inside the authenticated layout, after the sidebar).

**6. Wire the What's New page** — Add a route at `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/dashboard/whats-new/page.tsx` that renders the WhatsNew component, and add a "What's New" link in the sidebar. Read the sidebar component to find where navigation links are defined.

### Service type detection logic:
```typescript
// Determine user's service types
const [servers, hosting] = await Promise.all([
  db.server.findFirst({ where: { userId: user.id } }),
  db.hostingAccount.findFirst({ where: { userId: user.id } }),
]);
const userServices: string[] = [];
if (servers) {
  // Check if they have game servers vs regular VPS
  const hasGame = await db.server.findFirst({ where: { userId: user.id, gamePlanId: { not: null } } });
  if (hasGame) userServices.push("GAME");
  const hasVps = await db.server.findFirst({ where: { userId: user.id, gamePlanId: null } });
  if (hasVps) userServices.push("VPS");
}
if (hosting) userServices.push("HOSTING");
```

### Guardrails:
- Never expose infrastructure details, API keys, internal IPs, or server topology in announcements
- The body field is admin-authored Markdown — sanitize on render (no raw HTML injection)
- Screenshots should be referenced by relative path (e.g. /uploads/announcements/screenshot.png), not external URLs

### Style reference:
Match the existing Nxeon dark theme — look at any existing component in components/customer/ for the pattern:
- Background: navy-900, navy-950
- Cards: rounded-2xl/3xl, border border-white/[0.06], bg-gradient or bg-black/20
- Text: text-white for headings, text-slate-400 for secondary
- Accent: brand-500 (purple), accent-blue
- Buttons: btn-primary, btn-ghost, btn-danger classes

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` when done to verify no type errors.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

102	  // and only surface when the operator flips the flag. The pages/routes are never
103	  // removed; this only drops the nav entry, its sub-tabs and its ⌘K entries.
104	  const [showAgency, showAds] = await Promise.all([
105	    getSettingBool("feature_admin_agency", false),
106	    getSettingBool("feature_admin_ads", false),
107	  ]);
108	  const HIDDEN_SECTION_FLAGS: Record<string, boolean> = {
109	    agency: showAgency,
110	    ads: showAds,
111	  };
112	  const navSections = ADMIN_NAV.filter(
113	    (section) => HIDDEN_SECTION_FLAGS[section.key] !== false,
114	  );
115	
116	  // Filter every entry's members down to what this role can access, drop entries
117	  // that end up empty, then drop sections that end up empty. An entry always
118	  // links to (and its sub-tab bar always starts at) its first *accessible*
119	  // member, so no role is ever handed a link that just bounces it to /admin.
120	  const visibleSections = navSections.map((section) => ({
121	    ...section,
122	    entries: section.entries
123	      .map((entry) => ({
124	        ...entry,
125	        tabs: entry.tabs.filter((tab) => canAccessHref(user.role, tab.href)),
126	      }))
127	      .filter((entry) => entry.tabs.length > 0),
128	  })).filter((section) => section.entries.length > 0);
129	
130	  // Flat list of every href this role may reach — handed to <AdminSubTabs /> so
131	  // the in-page tab bars hide the same members the sidebar does.
132	  const allowedHrefs = visibleSections.flatMap((s) =>
133	    s.entries.flatMap((e) => e.tabs.map((t) => t.href))
134	  );

137	    where: { userId: user.id },
138	    orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
139	    take: 15,
140	  });
141	
142	  // Attention-count badges for the sidebar. Each count fails soft (→ 0) so a
143	  // missing model/table can never break the admin layout.
144	  const soft = (p: Promise<number>) => p.catch(() => 0);
145	  const [chatUnread, ticketsAwaiting, abuseOpen, feedbackNew, improvementsProposed, coldEmailUnread] = await Promise.all([
146	    // Live chat: conversations flagged unread for agents (same "needs a reply"
147	    // signal the chat inbox sorts/counts by — ChatConversation.unreadForAgent).
148	    soft(db.chatConversation.count({ where: { unreadForAgent: true } })),
149	    // Support desk: tickets awaiting a staff reply (open + customer replies),

151	    soft(db.ticket.count({ where: { status: { in: ["OPEN", "CUSTOMER_REPLY"] } } })),
152	    // Abuse queue: alerts still OPEN.
153	    soft(db.abuseAlert.count({ where: { status: "OPEN" } })),
154	    // Feedback: new (untriaged) reports.
155	    soft(db.feedback.count({ where: { status: "NEW" } })),
156	    // Improvements board: proposals awaiting the owner's approve/decline.
157	    soft(db.improvement.count({ where: { status: "PROPOSED" } })),
158	    // Cold email: unread replies in the reply inbox (Conversation.unread), same
159	    // "needs a reply" signal as live chat above.
160	    soft(db.conversation.count({ where: { unread: true } })),
161	  ]);
162	
163	  // Per-route attention counts, unchanged in meaning from the flat sidebar.
164	  const badges: Record<string, number> = {
165	    "/admin/chat": chatUnread,
166	    "/admin/support": ticketsAwaiting,
167	    "/admin/abuse": abuseOpen,
168	    "/admin/feedback": feedbackNew,
169	    "/admin/improvements": improvementsProposed,
170	    "/admin/coldemail/inbox": coldEmailUnread,
171	  };
172	  // Build the sidebar: one icon'd row per top-level ENTRY, grouped into labelled
173	  // sections. Secondary members ride along as `children` — the sidebar never
174	  // expands them (they're the page's sub-tabs), but they keep the parent row
175	  // highlighted while you're on one and keep ⌘K able to reach every route.
176	  // Attention counts ROLL UP: an entry shows the sum of its members' badges, and
177	  // <AdminSubTabs /> repeats each member's own count on its tab.
178	  const nav: NavSection[] = visibleSections.map((section) => ({
179	    key: section.key,
180	    label: section.label,
181	    items: section.entries.map((entry) => {
182	      const rollup = entry.tabs.reduce((sum, tab) => sum + (badges[tab.href] ?? 0), 0);
183	      return {
184	        label: entry.label,
185	        href: entry.tabs[0].href,
186	        icon: entry.icon,
187	        badge: rollup > 0 ? rollup : undefined,
188	        children: entry.tabs.map((tab) => ({
189	          label: tab.label,
190	          href: tab.href,
191	          badge: badges[tab.href] > 0 ? badges[tab.href] : undefined,
192	        })),
193	      };
194	    }),
195	  }));
196

Everything is in place. Here is a summary of what was built:

---

**Update Notifications System -- Complete**

**6 new files created:**

1. `/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/actions-announcements.ts` -- Server actions with all 7 functions:
   - `listAnnouncements()` -- admin: all announcements, ordered by createdAt desc
   - `createAnnouncement()` -- admin: creates DRAFT with title, body, serviceTypes[], screenshotUrl
   - `publishAnnouncement(id)` -- admin: sets PUBLISHED + publishedAt (the approval gate)
   - `unpublishAnnouncement(id)` -- admin: reverts to DRAFT
   - `deleteAnnouncement(id)` -- admin: cascading delete
   - `getUnseenAnnouncements()` -- customer: PUBLISHED + unseen + filtered by user's actual services (GAME/VPS/HOSTING/MAIL detection via Server.gamePlanId and HostingAccount)
   - `markAnnouncementSeen(id)` -- customer: upsert UserAnnouncementSeen
   - `getWhatsNew(serviceFilter?)` -- customer: all PUBLISHED with `seen` boolean flag

2. `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/admin/announcements/page.tsx` -- Admin page (area-gated "platform")

3. `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/admin/AnnouncementsAdmin.tsx` -- Admin client component with:
   - Create form (title, body textarea, service type checkboxes, screenshot path input)
   - Markdown preview panel using the existing `renderMarkdown` from lib/blog.ts
   - Announcement list with DRAFT (amber) / PUBLISHED (green) status badges
   - Publish / Unpublish / Delete action buttons
   - Seen-by count per announcement

4. `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/AnnouncementPopup.tsx` -- Login popup:
   - Fetches unseen announcements client-side on mount (soft-fails to nothing)
   - createPortal modal (same pattern as HeardAboutUsPrompt) at z-[70]
   - Shows announcements one at a time with "Next" / "Got it" button
   - Rendered Markdown body + screenshot display
   - Service type tags shown in header
   - Marks each as seen optimistically on dismiss

5. `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/WhatsNew.tsx` -- Full timeline feed:
   - Service type filter tabs (All / Game Servers / VPS / Hosting / Mail)
   - Each card shows timeline dot, date, title, rendered body, screenshot, service tags
   - "New" badge on unseen announcements
   - IntersectionObserver auto-marks announcements as seen after 2s in viewport
   - Empty state with sparkle icon when no announcements exist

6. `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/dashboard/whats-new/page.tsx` -- Dashboard route wrapper
